sections.label: Tax rebate and NOR scheme
sections.summary: A 50% income tax rebate capped at $200 is granted for YA 2019, and the NOR scheme lapses after YA 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, as part of the Bicentennial Bonus, a Personal Income Tax Rebate of 50% of income tax payable capped at $200 will be granted to all tax resident individuals for Year of Assessment (YA) 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, the Not Ordinarily Resident (NOR) scheme, which was introduced in Budget 2002, will lapse after YA 2020.

sections.label: Qualifying Funds tax concessions
sections.summary: Tax concessions for Qualifying Funds are extended until 31 December 2024 to grow asset management.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, to continue to grow Singapore’s asset management industry, the tax concessions relating to Qualifying Funds will be extended till 31 December 2024.

sections.label: Self-employed commission agents compliance
sections.summary: Compliance burden will be eased for self-employed commission agents earning gross annual commission income up to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, we will ease the compliance burden for individual tax residents who are self-employed commission agents and are earning gross annual commission income of up to $50,000.

sections.label: Grandparent Care Relief amendment
sections.summary: Clause 29 amends section 39 to broaden Grandparent Care Relief to working mothers with handicapped and unmarried children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, I welcome the amendment in clause 29 that amends section 39 of the current Act to broaden the Grandparent Care Relief to working mothers with "handicapped" and unmarried children.

sections.label: BIPS approval and extension
sections.summary: BIPS was approved in Budget 2016 for July 2016 to December 2018, then extended three years till December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: BIPS was approved during Budget 2016 for two and a half years from July 2016 to December 2018, and then extended for three more years till December 2021.

sections.label: BIPS volunteering hours figures
sections.summary: Between July 2016 and December 2017, 48 businesses contributed about 17,000 volunteering hours through BIPS projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In response to my Parliamentary Question in November 2018, we know then that between July 2016 and December 2017, or 1.5 years, only 48 businesses contributed about 17,000 volunteering hours through BIPS projects.

sections.label: Disbursing tax deduction limit to IPCs
sections.summary: The scheme could be made fully flexible by disbursing the $50,000 tax deduction limit to each IPC to use as they deem fit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given that, the scheme could be made fully flexible through disbursing the $50,000 tax deduction limit to each IPC and allowing them to use the funds as they deem fit.

sections.label: BIPS salary-based tax deduction problems
sections.summary: BIPS offers tax deductions based on actual employee salary rates, which could be problematic due to sensitive information disclosure and lack of audit knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, the current BIPS offers tax deductions based on the actual salary rates of the employees of the businesses which could be problematic given (a) the need to disclose such sensitive information and (b) BIPS do not have the industry knowledge and/or bandwidth to audit salary figures given by corporate partners to determine if they are true and fairly reported.

sections.label: US and France food donation deductions
sections.summary: In the US companies can claim 15% tax deduction of taxable income for donated food; in France up to 60% tax rebate depending on expiry date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the US, companies can claim 15% tax deduction of their taxable income based on the value of the donated food.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In France, if a company makes a food donation to a registered charity, they can claim up to 60% of the value of the food as a tax rebate, depending on how near it is to the food’s expiry date.

sections.label: BIPS enhancements fixed manhour rate
sections.summary: BIPS enhancements include an option to claim tax deductions on wages based on fixed manhour rates, with higher rates for skill-based volunteerism and a safe harbour for related expenses under 5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Among the enhancements made to BIPS, we will, as Ms Anthea Ong highlighted, provide an option for businesses to claim tax deductions on wages based on a fixed manhour rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The fixed manhour rates will be differentiated with a higher rate for skill-based volunteerism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To further simplify the administrative process, we will be introducing a "safe harbour" for related expenses, such that IPCs need not verify supporting documentation for related expenses that make up less than 5% of the total qualifying expenditure.
